observable_outcome: M8's self-update design is fixed in writing and measurable against the tree it describes: docs/operations/self-update.md states all six decisions in full - where the Ed25519 release private key lives (owner release machine only, outside the repository), the per-machine trust anchor as a fixed-path, mode-checked, multi-key set the Bootstrapper resolves itself instead of accepting on argv, and the Cloud KMS path that leaves the verify path untouched; why manifest digest, signature and V2-021's source bundle digest are three different claims of which all three are needed, and how bundle_digest, candidate_id and contract_release join a running binary to the gated source tree as manifest data rather than a component edge; how the Bootstrapper stays independent (separate binary, go/ast import guard, bootstrap run launcher, per-launch re-verification, child restart) and where the regress stops; the five coordinates of the module version manifest and the machine-local installed record; the schema-interval intersection invariant bounding the unavoidable mixed-version period, which is exactly the coexist stage; the concrete Firestore operation at each of expand, coexist, migrate and contract, with contract as the first irreversible stage and the measured record_schema equality gap that makes envelope coexist impossible today; the GC predicate that reproduces release.RetentionEligible's refusals by value plus the two refusals that make 'cannot delete while the rollback window is open' follow from the manifest; and the four-way rollback window with its recorded closure and irreversibility list. The document also carries the measured baseline, the eleven-item gap list, the local-closure/preview-local/preview-gcp classification mapped onto roadmap M8's four completion conditions, the V2-034/V2-035 boundary, and escalations E1-E4. No code changes. .agents/v2/evidence/V2-033-update.json is registered in the evidence index and make check is green on the committed tree.
acceptance_criteria: A1. docs/operations/self-update.md is rewritten (it is 14 lines today) so that each of the six required decisions has its own titled section and is decided, not surveyed. (1) Signed Runner bundle: the single Ed25519 private key lives only on the owner's release machine at an owner-only 0600 path outside the repository, the workspace, any data root, any bundle and any evidence record; the trust anchor is its public half, replicated out of band to each machine as a 0400 file at a fixed absolute path under the machine configuration root, holding one accepted entry per line as 'key_id algorithm base64(pubkey)' so that rotation across two never-shared machines is add-then-remove rather than a flag day; the Cloud KMS phase moves only the signer, because the anchor stays a public key file and internal/update's verify path does not change. (2) Independent Bootstrapper. (3) Module version manifest. (4) Schema expand-coexist-migrate-contract. (5) Old binary GC. (6) Rollback window. Each section states the decision, the mechanism, and what a violation looks like.

A2. The fail-closed guarantee is written as a list of refusals with the measured defect it replaces. State that cmd/bootstrap install currently takes --public-key <path> and hands whatever it reads to update.Install, so a caller who chooses the key defeats the signature entirely; that V2-034 must resolve the anchor from the fixed machine path; and that the launcher exits non-zero without touching versions/ and without starting any child when the anchor is absent, is not a regular file, is not owned by the invoking user, has a mode wider than 0600, is empty, or parses to zero entries. Name internal/runner/confinement.go's NamespaceConfinement.Probe/ErrNamespaceUnsupported as the refusal idiom being reused, so the Runner side has one fail-closed shape rather than two.

A3. The digest/signature relationship is answered explicitly, not left open: Manifest.BinarySHA256 binds manifest to binary bytes and is the only thing that lets a launcher re-verify bytes already on disk; the Ed25519 signature over manifest||sha256(binary) binds that pair to the owner's key and answers a question no digest can answer, because an attacker who replaces the binary replaces its digest too; V2-021's BundleDigest is sha256 over the framing role\0path\0sha256\n of seven source roles and contains no binary at all. All three are required, and the document states the measured hole they leave (nothing joins a signed binary to a gated source tree) and its closure: bundle_digest, candidate_id and contract_release become signed manifest fields, copied in at build time as values, so internal/release still never imports internal/update and internal/update stays standard-library-only.

A4. Manifest schema evolution is decided. Record the measured constraint that Verify requires exact equality with 'agentic-loop/module-manifest/v1' and decodes with DisallowUnknownFields, so any added field makes an installed Bootstrapper reject every new bundle - the one component that cannot auto-update. Decide the one-time bump to '.../v2' carrying the A3 fields while no Stable and no installed Bootstrapper exist, and the permanent replacement of the single constant with an ordered accepted set, so later evolution is itself expand-coexist-migrate-contract at the manifest level. State the expiry condition of that licence: once any Bootstrapper is placed on a machine, the accepted-set change must land first in its own release with the old id still accepted.

A5. Bootstrapper independence is written as a structural property with the guard that enforces it. The Runner must not link internal/update at all (measured: only cmd/bootstrap/main.go and internal/release/source_guard_test.go reference it); V2-034 adds a go/ast import guard asserting no file under cmd/runner/** or internal/runner/** imports internal/update and that internal/update's non-test files import only the standard library. Record the measured gap that cmd/bootstrap has verbs install|switch|--version only and nothing in the tree reads root/stable, so 'recover from the Stable launcher' has no implementation; and define bootstrap run --channel stable|preview as resolving root/<channel> to versions/<v>, re-verifying versions/<v>/runner against versions/<v>/manifest.json before every exec, probing confinement, and starting the Runner as a child in its own process group. Define an update as: parent installs side by side, flips the symlink, stops the child, starts a new child - the replaced process never installs and never execs itself. Answer 'recover from the Stable launcher' concretely: which process reads the anchor set, which reads the stable symlink and the version manifest, which re-verifies bytes, and that canonical state is touched by none of them.

A6. The regress stops where the document says it stops. State that a bundle has no bootstrapper role and the launcher refuses one; that replacing the launcher or changing the anchor set is an owner-attended per-machine procedure that does not pass through the Loop's promotion gate; and why stopping there is acceptable - the launcher has no network, no Provider, no canonical store and no workspace, and its entire input set is (anchor set, bundle bytes, root path, channel). Cite docs/architecture/technology.md's existing decision rather than reopening it.

A7. The module version manifest is enumerated: binary (version, binary_sha256); canonical schema interval [schema_min, schema_max], stated as the coexist mechanism and not a validation detail; contract (contract_release, contract_digest, runner_api_min, runner_api_max); bundle (bundle_digest, candidate_id); provenance (key_id, algorithm). Separately define root/state/installed.json as machine-local and never canonical: installed versions with install time and interval, current stable and preview targets, previous stable, last switch with its reason, rolled_back_at, window_closed_at and the criterion that closed it - written after the filesystem operation it describes so a crash leaves it stale-but-safe. Say why it is machine-local: machines are not shared, so a canonical 'what is installed' record would be wrong on both machines for most of every update.

A8. The mixed-version period is declared unavoidable and bounded. State the invariant: at every instant the current canonical schema lies inside the intersection of the [schema_min, schema_max] intervals of every version any machine can currently route to (stable, preview, previous stable, both machines); a version may be switched onto a machine only if the canonical schema is inside its interval; the canonical schema advances only into the intersection; an advance that would empty it is refused, not scheduled. Split enforcement honestly: V2-034 enforces the single-machine half at the launcher and records intervals in installed.json; the cross-machine half needs the Control Plane to know each Runner's running version, which measurably does not exist (internal/api carries only a static response 'schema_version':'v1' and optimistic-concurrency Expected*Version fields, no version on any Runner-facing request; internal/domain has no Runner aggregate, only a RunnerID string type). That is escalation E1 and is not V2-034's work. Also state the distinction that Preview/Stable routing is per Repository while binary version is per machine, and that a Runner API compatibility break is expressed by runner_api_min/max, not by conflating the two.

A9. The four schema stages are written as concrete operations on the measured Firestore codec ({record_schema, kind, payload-as-JSON-string}; RecordSchema is the constant 'v1'; DecodeRecord at store.go:79 and decodeDocument at store.go:173 both refuse with ErrInvalidSchema on inequality; payload decode is a plain json.Unmarshal so unknown fields are ignored and absent fields default). EXPAND: write the new payload field alongside the old under the unchanged record_schema, no reader change needed, canonical schema N to N+1, the new binary declares [N, N+1]. COEXIST: both binaries run, every reader resolves 'new field if present else old field'; this period is exactly the mixed-version window of A8 and the document must state that correspondence. MIGRATE: bounded, resumable, idempotent backfill shaped like a reconcile tick (at most 100 documents and 30 s per tick, restart from a stored cursor, no unbounded query, no wall-clock dependence). CONTRACT: stop writing and delete the old field, bumping record_schema only where the envelope must change; always a separate Increment from its expand.

A10. The reversibility boundary is explicit: rollback is possible during expand, coexist and migrate and impossible after contract, because a binary whose schema_max is below the post-contract schema can no longer read the store, so the contract step itself closes that version's rollback window. Contract may run only when every still-routable version, plus the current and previous stable, has schema_min at or above the post-contract schema - the same predicate as GC eligibility, used a second time. Record the measured blocker for the envelope half: both readers compare record_schema with !=, so a bumped envelope is invisible to the current reader and envelope coexist is impossible today; widening to an accepted set is itself the envelope's expand step and belongs to the store-firestore component, which is escalation E2 and blocks V2-035's shared-state rollback condition. State that V2-034 proves the four stages against an injected codec port with an in-package fake, and must not edit internal/store/firestore/**.

A11. The GC predicate is written so that 'cannot delete while the rollback window is open' follows from the manifest. Reproduce release.RetentionEligible's four outcomes by value (current stable target; previous stable target; rollback window still open against an injected clock and a contract-declared duration, never the clock alone; a Requirement's StableSnapshot still references it), and add the two refusals that only exist once binaries are real: the version is the target of any channel symlink on this machine, including preview, which RetentionEligible does not model; and deleting it would leave no retained version whose [schema_min, schema_max] contains the current canonical schema. State that internal/update re-expresses rather than imports the predicate (dp-v2-021 d12 forbids the edge, and V2-034 adds the mirror-image guard inside internal/update), with a case-by-case agreement test on identical inputs. Give the crash-safe deletion order: re-read every channel symlink immediately before deleting, refuse if the target is reachable, rename the directory aside, remove it, then update installed.json. State that because the bundle carries that version's Stable and Preview documents, this single predicate is also what satisfies release-contract.md section 5's document retention - there is no second rule.

A12. The rollback window is defined as a conjunction with recorded closure. It stays open while any of these holds: the version is the previous stable route target (generation); no contract-stage step has moved the canonical schema outside its interval (schema stage); a contract-declared minimum dwell has not elapsed on an injected clock since the successor became Stable (time); the successor does not yet hold a passed Preview capability exercise for the whole Release Contract (evidence). Closure requires all four to have ceased and is written as window_closed_at plus the closing criterion; nothing recomputes it from the wall clock at read time. State what becomes irreversible: the binary and its bundled documents become GC-eligible, so after deletion returning to that version needs a rebuild and a re-sign and the cheap symlink rollback is gone; and if a schema contract step closed the window, the store no longer serves a shape that version can read, which is the only one-way transition in M8. Also record that update.Switch measurably has the ping-pong defect dp-v2-021 d8 removed from release.Router - it flips stable to any installed version with no record, no monotonicity and no gate - and that V2-034 must mirror the fix: record every switch with its reason, refuse a second consecutive rollback, and require the forward direction to name a gate-passed candidate digest.

A13. The document carries the classification table and checks it against the roadmap. Local closure (V2-034, hermetic): fail-closed anchor and signature refusals; the three-digest join as manifest data; the accepted-manifest-schema set; the import guards; bootstrap run with per-launch re-verification and child restart; the manifest fields and the single-machine interval check; the four stages and the reversibility boundary over the injected port; the GC predicate and crash-safe deletion; the rollback window predicate and recorded closure; the monotonic Switch. preview-local (V2-035): the new Loop deploying its own next version to Preview; breaking a real Preview Control Plane and Runner and recovering through the Stable launcher; rolling back without losing shared canonical state; two roots or machines on different versions both making progress. preview-gcp (D1/V2-054, beyond M8): KMS-backed signing, Artifact Registry distribution, the deploy path. Then map roadmap M8's four completion conditions: condition 1 preview-local (V2-035); condition 2 preview-local (V2-035), justified by release-contract.md section 3 clause 2 because it is a Loop-own-behaviour condition, so it is not D1's; condition 3 preview-local (V2-035) and blocked on E2; condition 4 local closure (V2-034). State plainly that none of release-contract.md section 3's four preview-gcp-only items is named by an M8 completion condition, so M8 closes at preview-local.

A14. The V2-034/V2-035 boundary is written claim by claim. V2-034 owns internal/update and cmd/bootstrap plus the runbook, and must not deploy anything, start a real Provider CLI, touch GCP or a credential, or report M8 conditions 1 to 3 as met; its honest claim is that the local closure refuses the wrong bundle, launches only a re-verified binary, keeps a rollback target and its documents while the window is open, and cannot delete or contract past a still-routable version. V2-035 adds no update semantics: if it needs a new refusal or manifest field it stops and escalates, because a semantics change found during a live exercise invalidates the local evidence it was built on. V2-035's evidence must record environment class preview-local, machine identifiers for both roots or machines, emulator name and version, kernel version, Provider CLI versions where used, and skip count zero. The document also states the trap that a launcher restarting a child in a unit test is not M8 condition 2: V2-034 may only claim 'the launcher re-execs a re-verified binary after the child exits'.

A15. The measured baseline and the eleven-item gap list appear in the document, each item naming the file and symbol it was measured from, with the argv used: (1) no launcher or exec path (verbs install|switch|--version; nothing reads root/stable); (2) trust anchor from argv --public-key with no path, ownership, mode, key-set or key-id checks; (3) no re-verification of on-disk bytes before exec; (4) Switch is an unguarded symlink flip with no record, monotonicity or gate requirement; (5) no GC and no retention state, so versions/ grows without bound and there is no rolled_back_at, window state or installed-version record; (6) the manifest is closed and single-module and carries no bundle_digest, candidate_id, contract_release, runner_api range, key_id or algorithm; (7) no schema migration machinery anywhere and no owner for the canonical schema counter, while both Firestore readers compare record_schema with !=; (8) no version reporting (no domain Runner aggregate, no version field on any Runner-facing request); (9) cmd/bootstrap has no test files although make component-runner runs ./cmd/bootstrap, and internal/update has exactly two tests (TestInstallSwitchAndRollbackKeepBothVersions, TestVerifyRejectsTamperAndIncompatibleSchema) with no fail-closed negative case beyond tamper and schema interval; (10) the launcher does not consult runner.NamespaceConfinement.Probe; (11) no audit record of install or switch. Also record escalations E1 (Runner version reporting), E2 (store-firestore accepted record_schema set, blocking V2-035), E3 (Cloud KMS Ed25519 availability is a D1-time fact, so the anchor set must allow a second algorithm) and E4 (docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md section 5 names only the update component for M8, but the launcher lives in cmd/bootstrap, a runner component root, so V2-034 should emit both an update and a runner record as V2-058 did). None of E1 to E4 may be resolved by editing ci/components.json, the Makefile, go.mod, go.sum or devbox.*.

A16. No code changes and no fabricated claims. devbox run --pure -- git status --porcelain and git diff --name-only show changes confined to docs/operations/self-update.md, .agents/v2/evidence/V2-033-update.json and .agents/v2/evidence/index.json. Existing tests keep their names and pass with no test file edited; the measured baseline to state is two top-level tests in internal/update and '[no test files]' for cmd/bootstrap. The document contains no key material, no secret value, no token and no credential, and no digest value that would create the self-referential fixpoint dp-v2-021 d14 prohibits - docs/operations is deliberately outside V2-021's documentation bundle role (docs/preview/**.md and docs/stable/**.md), which is why measured facts may live there. The document must not claim that any Preview was deployed, that any capability was exercised in a Preview environment, that any real Provider CLI, GCP project, KMS key or credential was used, or that any recovery or rollback was observed: V2-033 is a design task and its only executed checks are the read-only measurements and the make targets named in the validation section.

A17. Determinism is passed on as an acceptance property for V2-034 and honoured here: the document requires of V2-034 no fixed sleep, no wall-clock dependence, no background timer, no goroutine in tests, bounded deadline polling only, an injected clock, one top-level function per journey, t.TempDir fixtures and no dependence on another test's order; and it states that a result which needed a retry to pass is a stop-and-escalate condition, not a pass. V2-033 itself reports no check it did not execute, and a skipped check is recorded with status skipped and is never counted as a pass (gate rule G7). Record the execution environment identifier (uname -srm, go version, devbox environment) in the evidence record.

A18. Exactly one evidence record: .agents/v2/evidence/V2-033-update.json, id ev-v2-033-update, task_id V2-033 as the producer, correlation_id v2-033-self-update-design, component update, result passed, with one check per acceptance item above carrying the argv actually executed, the working directory and the timeout. Its evidence_key is the update component key read with devbox run --pure -- make evidence-keys on the final tree at which devbox run --pure -- make check (format included) is green; read the key on that final tree after git add, because the git ls-files-based input set omits untracked new files and a formatting-only change moves keys. State honestly in a check summary that this task changes no file under internal/update/**, so the update component key is unmoved and this record is a design-only record whose claim is 'the design document exists, agrees with the measured tree, and the update component check is green', not that any new behaviour was proven. One check summary additionally reports the docs and task-ledger component keys from the same evidence-keys run, because this task's edits move those two. Register exactly one appended entry in .agents/v2/evidence/index.json (id, task_id V2-033, component update, result passed, release_eligible false, evidence_hash equal to the sha256 of the record file's final committed bytes, path), touching no other task's entry, and confirm devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/contracts is green with the record in place. That pair - registered in the index and the ledger test green - is the definition of done, not merely that the commands ran.

A19. Commit the evidence first, then confirm devbox run --pure -- make check is green on the committed state, because gitleaks git scans committed history and never an uncommitted working tree. Checkpoints are pushed one at a time by the coordinator, with the parent commit's v2 selective CI confirmed green before the next push, per docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md section 10.
